text:
evan: quick brain-dump: after yesterday's EU saturation event i'm thinking we should formalize a "detour-as-a-service" layer instead of ad-hoc proxy rules. the goal: single place to reason about residency, sensitivity, quality, and cost. reactions?
maria: +1. current logic is scattered between proxy, router, and console. a service makes sense. what would the interface look like?
evan: rough sketch: request comes to edge proxy -> proxy calls detour-service with headers (tenant, residency_hint, sensitivity, route_slo) -> detour-service returns either {accept_local}, {detour: target_region, model_policy, cache_warmup:true/false, reason_code} or {reject, reason}. proxy then enforces.
kevin: can we avoid an extra RPC on the hot path? adding a network hop could add 5-10ms. maybe detour-service exposes a local fast-cache in the proxy (ttl=1s) and async sync.
sophia: i think that's fine if we do admission-only decisions. we already pay a few ms for auth and token checks. but make it configurable per tenant (low-latency tenants bypass).
josh: operational notes: need a leader election for global detour decision so we don't have inconsistent targets. but i'd prefer a deterministic algorithm: detour-service computes ordered region list based on capacity and tenant policy. no cross-node leader required.
maria: important: telemetry fields. we must emit: detour_applied (bool), detour_reason, original_region, target_region, model_swap (bool), kv_prefetch_triggered (bool), quality_eval_id (if any). also add billing tags so finance can map cost delta.
evan: +1. also add a detour_ttl header so downstream logs know this was a detour decision for X seconds.
kevin: security/legal: what are allowed transforms to payload? are we allowed to strip metadata or hash IDs before leaving region?
sophia: legal-bot what do we need here?
legal-bot: quick note from legal: any detour that moves data outside of a resident jurisdiction requires either (a) tenant opt-in, or (b) tenant contract clause for global processing. anonymization (hashing) helps but not sufficient for regulated datasets. recommend default: opt-in for EU resident tenants.
maria: OK. so detour-service must return "policy_violation" if tenant disallows. also add tenant-scoped toggles in org-config.
kevin: implementation detail: model downgrade mapping should be tenant-configurable and versioned. we should store allowed_downgrades as pairs with a quality-loss estimate. that lets console show expected delta.
evan: regarding KV cache prewarm: idea: if detour-service plans to detour tenant T to region R, emit a prewarm job that warms top-N prefixes for the tenant on R. this is async and best-effort. estimate costs first.
josh: prewarm could be heavy. suggest heuristics: only prewarm when historical detour rate > X or when tenant traffic > Y qps. otherwise accept cold-cache penalty.
sophia: rollout: start with an 'administrative' detour mode where detour-service only suggests decisions to ops (no enforcement). then enable admission-time enforcement for opt-in tenants. canary on 1% traffic.
evan: metrics for A/B: latency p50/p95, model-quality delta (gold prompts), token-cost delta, kv-miss-rate, customer complaint rate. need a short-term quality metric we can compute automatically (e.g., semantic-similarity to baseline).

evidence: sample header contract (proto):
```
GET /detour/decide?tenant_id=acme&residency_hint=eu&model=llama-2-13b
Headers:
  X-Request-ID: 123
  X-Redwood-Sensitivity: low
Response 200:
  X-Detour-Decision: detour
  X-Detour-Target: us-west-2
  X-Detour-Model-Policy: downgrade=llama-2-7b
  X-Detour-Reason: capacity
  X-Detour-TTL: 60
```
kevin: proxy will need to transform response into internal routing actions. and logs must include these headers.
maria: UX: console needs a "detour insights" page per-tenant with timeline, counts, and toggle. also a "what-if" simulator to preview cost/quality tradeoffs.
josh: alarms: create a new SLO for detour error rate (<0.1%) and a runbook for cascading detours. also track cross-region hop count.
sophia: edge case: what about in-flight requests when region capacity drops after admission? we decided admission-only, but we should consider a graceful degrade if the serving pool starts OOM. maybe a per-request kill switch from runtime to mark "retryable" which proxy handles by re-submitting through detour-service. risky though.
kevin: agree risky. prefer controller do nothing mid-request except if runtime explicitly returns RETRYABLE_DOWNSCALE. then proxy can re-run admission via detour-service. record this in metrics.
evan: action items: evan -> write RFC follow-up 'detour-as-a-service' draft with interface and failure modes; kevin -> prototype proxy fast-cache and headers; maria -> console wireframes and metrics list; josh -> operational limits and prewarm cost estimate; sophia -> coordinate legal consent flow with legal-bot.
deploy-bot: starting 1% canary (staging) to validate detour-service latency and header roundtrip. will report in 10m. :robot_face:
legal-bot: uploaded short consent template (detour-consent-v1) to drive.
deploy-bot: canary results (partial): 10m window: detour-rpc-latency p50=3ms p95=12ms, detour_applied=34, model_downgrades=8, avg-latency delta +18ms for detoured requests, kv-miss-rate +9%.
maria: cool. i'm happy to co-author RFC. evan tag me when you start.
evan: will do. thanks all. reconvene in RFC doc comments. :calendar:
